title: Profile: Add Meta Information to profiles
description:
If a file called "profile.json" is present in the profile directory, the information
for "author" and "version" is being displayed directly in the profile screen. If no
information is present, the fields are left empty.

Additionally, a field called "email" may be added, which will be displayed as a tooltip
for the author information

notes.body:
@stigbjorlykke would you do me a favor and take a look at the functionality? 

To head off the discussion, I opted for the json format, as it will allow the addition of special characters as well as longer information and is a better tool to work with as our usual files. I know this deviates a little from the general information we have, but in the long-run should provide us with the greater benefits.

Also, I will add description to the file as well, as soon as I figure out a good mechanism to display it. Currently, all ideas lead to very ugly dialogs.

I also recognize, that this will only work in the UI, but so will the rest of the system anyway
For a short preview, take a look here: ![Profile Detail](/uploads/438e314d5b7b70e3ebf951d79a3f4f99/Screenshot_20210909_104536.png)
I really like having an author field.
I am thinking, that adding that information in Wireshark would not be required. So it would be ok to edit the .json file by hand. Is that ok?
Ok as long as it's documented - [Configuration Profiles](https://www.wireshark.org/docs/wsug_html/#ChCustConfigProfilesSection)

added 1 commit
  • 4aa34daa - Profile: Add Meta Information to profiles
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/4147/diffs?diff_id=243071662&start_sha=2b81acd0816c403b85c4b26e60e66cb690da1387)

One thing, that will not be solved by this is, that when you copy a profile, it will not copy the profile.json file. That actually makes somewhat sense, but it may be confusing at first, as we copy everything else. We could add a blank file instead, which could then be filled by the user. What do you guys think?
Why would not default be to copy if it exists so original author info comes over?

Is there a bigger plan for more fields?  
Not that it is easy to answer but what constitutes a change to a Profile and when is it no longer the Version listed?  
Even after taking Betty's Profile class, my `Default` profiles are more like the [Ship of Theseus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ship_of_Theseus).

My assumption here is, that the version is a field for the original author of the profile, which will allow him/her to keep track of the version of profile used by a user in a class or office setup. We coul dof-course implement some form of automatic mechanism, in which - if the user copies/moves/updates the profile, so that it's files change - the version information is automatically updated. This is a future thing, as of right now, it is a strict, author provided information.
I will have a look early next week.

Some initial notes.

When starting to use a copied profile it will very quick be out of sync with the original profile, and then this information will be very misleading (first of all the version, but also the author when the profile is completely changed). This should be indicated somewhere, that this is the version and author it was initially copied from. This is one of the reasons why I don't think this is a good idea, and why I did not add this in the first place.

1. Is it possible to not show the Version and Author columns when not having profiles using profile.json? I'm not that interested in this information, and my columns will only have default information.

2. I don't think the version should be listed for Default and Global profiles, because it's just the same version string for everything.

3. In Lua scripts we have some more entries in the "plugin info". Maybe we should start having the same entries in this file for consistency?
  - "version" with a string value identifying the plugin version (required)
  - "description" with a string value describing the plugin (optional)
  - "author" with a string value of the author's name(s) (optional)
  - "repository" with a string value of a URL to a repository (optional)

4. It should be possible to show a complete list of all this entries, not only for profiles but also equally for Lua plugins.

5. If adding a "repository" entry it should be possible to "Update from source".

> When starting to use a copied profile it will very quick be out of sync with the original profile, and then this information will be very misleading (first of all the version, but also the author when the profile is completely changed). This should be indicated somewhere, that this is the version and author it was initially copied from. This is one of the reasons why I don't think this is a good idea, and why I did not add this in the first place.

That is partially true. As soon as you update the profile (by changing settings) you would be out-of-sync. One way to circumvent this would be, to treat profiles with this .json file as "system" profiles and the user would need to copy from them in order to change things, same way we do with the internal ones.

> Is it possible to not show the Version and Author columns when not having profiles using profile.json? I'm not that interested in this information, and my columns will only have default information.

Sure, we could also make the columns configurable and opt for the user to hide the information. Trick here would be to storing that information, so it in itself would not be a profile information, but making this a general info would make sense in this case.

> I don't think the version should be listed for Default and Global profiles, because it's just the same version string for everything.

Well, it makes sense screenshot wise, but sure, I can hide that information.

> "repository" with a string value of a URL to a repository (optional)

I am thinking exactly along those lines for future updates, 

> It should be possible to show a complete list of all this entries, not only for profiles but also equally for Lua plugins.

May I ask, what your connection between profiles and Lua plugins is here? As far as I am aware, only profiles show up in this dialog? Or was that a thinking, to combine a method for having additional information shared between items like profiles and Lua plugins? If so, I would rather not do that, as we might have similar fields now, but may differ in the future. And to handle both in the same way just unnecessarily complicates things.

> If adding a "repository" entry it should be possible to "Update from source".

Yes, that would be a future update, but would make more sense if the profile is static, right?

Docs for No.3 above.  
Wireshark Dev Guide - Lua Global/Utility Functions: 
[set_plugin_info(table)](https://www.wireshark.org/docs/wsdg_html_chunked/lua_module_Utility.html#global_functions_Utility)  
Set a Lua table with meta-data about the plugin, such as version.

Thanks for the link. Still, for me those are two completely different sets of information, not necessarily the same thing. In which case it is ok for me, if they are presented with different information

So we are thinking about adding a third group: Personal, Global and "Contrib" (name to be discussed). The last one will behave like a Global profile and this is all profiles having a "profile.json" file. Ok, that sounds like a plan, but may involve some extra work. Like where to store, how to handle duplicate profile names etc.

Hidden column information can be stored in recent_common, which is not profile dependent.

Regarding the link to Lua plugins: here I was thinking about using the same pattern to display the entries both for a Profile and a Lua plugin. The UI should be as similar as possible. Currently Lua plugins only show version, not the others.

That works for me.  I like the point @stigbjorlykke Stig made, that once they have copied it becomes theirs/Personal and any author info should either be wiped at first change, or chained. BettyD/1stNewPerson/2ndNewPerson.  Chaining would be cool, but would probably be a pain to implement so strike that.  Perhaps the best thing would be dialog when they import asking "This profile comes from X, would you like to change that to your name?"  This idea would only work in the GUI, but I figure it they know how to find the folder with all of the files in it, they will figure out how to change the author if they want.

I think the column in the screenshot that Roland started the thread with is fabulous @rknall But I'm against adding columns as mentioned in Stig's initial notes @stigbjorlykke. Ironic since I love columns.  But if a user doesn't see them because they are hidden, what is the point?  And if they are not hidden, most users are going to hide them straight away.
